subject.title: fix(discord): bound event listener slots after timeout

question: Should a timed-out but uncancellable Discord listener retain its concurrency slot indefinitely, accepting possible queue saturation in order to make `maxConcurrency` a strict bound on actual listener work?
rationale: Both policies are defensible but incompatible: releasing on timeout preserves queue progress while permitting background concurrency to exceed the limit, whereas retaining the slot enforces the limit but allows permanently hung listeners to stop gateway-event progress.

options.title: Enforce strict listener bound
options.body: Accept slot retention through actual settlement, require real-runtime recovery proof, and treat queue saturation as the intentional operational behavior.

options.title: Preserve timeout progress
options.body: Keep timeout-based slot release and close or redesign this PR because forward progress is more important than bounding uncancellable background listeners.

options.title: Design cancellable dispatch
options.body: Pause this PR and introduce an owner-approved cancellation contract so timeout can both stop listener work and release capacity safely.

recommendation.title: Enforce strict listener bound
recommendation.body: Accept slot retention through actual settlement, require real-runtime recovery proof, and treat queue saturation as the intentional operational behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: This person is the strongest available current-main Discord runtime routing candidate for deciding the event-queue timeout contract.
